title: Graded Entitlement Bands with Emergency Overage Circuit-breaker PRD
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers with bursty workloads need predictable entitlement behavior: soft tiers that allow short bursts, graded throttling/pacing for medium sustained spikes, and an automated emergency overage circuit-breaker that prevents noisy neighbors from causing marketplace-wide billing surprises. This PRD defines graded entitlement bands, per-plan pacing rates, and an emergency overage circuit-breaker that 1) automatically detects abnormal spend/throughput patterns, 2) enforces temporary conservative limits, and 3) provides an operator/tenant-visible remediation and crediting path. Goal: Reduce billing surprises, contain runaway workloads without immediate manual intervention, and provide transparent, auditable behavior for entitlements and overages.
background: Current entitlement model uses a single soft burst window + hard quota. That model struggles with multi-tenant burst patterns and introduces either unnecessary throttling or expensive emergency manual interventions. Several recent incidents produced large invoices for customers and a spike in support tickets. Product and Billing Ops want a safer default that balances developer experience with cost containment.
scope: In scope: design of graded entitlement bands (base, elevated, burst), pacing rules per band, automatic transitions between bands, emergency overage detector heuristics, circuit-breaker behavior and rollback, billing credit workflow integration, metrics to surface per-tenant pacing and overage events in Console, acceptance criteria and test plan. Implementation will include API contract changes for plan definitions and Console UI surfaces for monitoring and manual overrides.
out_of_scope: Out of scope: changes to core token metering logic, per-model compute pricing formulas, marketplace listing changes, long-term refunds manual review workflows (beyond immediate automated crediting stub), and on-prem private deployment billing connectors (handled in separate Private billing initiative).
requirements_summary: 1) Define three entitlement bands with clear thresholds and signal sources. 2) Implement per-tenant pacing enforcement: token/sec and concurrent call soft limits per band with smooth degrade (leaky-bucket). 3) Create an emergency overage detector using combined signal of spend velocity, real-time token/sec delta, and retention of historical baseline. 4) Circuit-breaker: on detection, reduce to conservative default band, flag tenant, emit events, and optionally apply automated credits. 5) Add Console UI for visibility and manual override with audit trail. 6) Ensure billing ledger records both normal usage and circuit-breaker adjustments for accounting.
acceptance_criteria: Policy: Entitlement bands defined in product catalog with machine-readable contract (band name, thresholds, pacing rates, grace window)
Enforcement: System throttles/paces traffic to the configured per-band limits while preserving low-latency for API calls that stay within limits
Detection: Emergency detector triggers within 5 minutes of sustained spend rate > 3x baseline for a tenant or absolute spend > 3x plan expected capacity
Circuit-breaker behavior: On trigger, tenant is moved to conservative pacing band automatically; all related events are recorded and visible in Console within 1 minute
Automation: Automated crediting proto is applied for clearly anomalous events and appears on the invoice as a line-item adjustment
Observability: Console shows per-tenant band, pacing metrics, and a timeline of transitions; alerts created for Billing Ops when a circuit-breaker fires
Backward compatibility: Existing plan definitions continue to work; new band definitions are additive and default mappings exist for legacy plans
Security and audit: Manual overrides are RBAC-restricted and generate an immutable audit entry
Billing ledger: Overages and credit adjustments are persisted in the ledger and reconciled by billing jobs without data loss
Performance: Enforcement path adds <5ms median latency overhead to token scoring in the critical path
success_metrics: Reduction in high-severity billing incident count by 70% in first quarter post-launch
Decrease in average invoice surprise percentage for flagged tenants by 60%
Time-to-detect anomalous spend reduced from hours to under 5 minutes
Operator mean-time-to-resolve for overage incidents reduced by 50%
Adoption: 40% of mid-market customers mapped to graded bands within 3 months
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature flags + shadow enforcement for 4 weeks on a subset of tenants (billing and metrics only). Phase 2: Opt-in beta for high-risk customers with operator review and manual override enabled. Phase 3: Gate-enabled default for new customers and opt-out for existing customers for 8 weeks. Phase 4: Full enforcement and automated crediting by release date. Each phase includes postmortem window and rollback plan.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics: per-tenant token/sec, spend velocity, band transitions, circuit-breaker firings, manual overrides. Dashboards: Tiered overview + detail per-tenant drill-down. Alerts: P0 page to Billing Ops on circuit-breaker; P1 Slack notif for high-frequency transitions. Retention: event traces stored for 90 days for investigations.
budget_and_pricing_formula: Define pricing knobs: base per-token rate unchanged. Introduce 'pacing surcharge' for elevated sustained throughput (applied per-minute while in elevated band) and a capped emergency fee for circuit-breaker events that is refundable if automated crediting determines anomaly. Billing formula must ensure predictable cost signals while avoiding double-billing during circuit-breaker adjustments.
api_and_billing_changes: Product API: new /plans/{id}/bands endpoint to retrieve band definitions; plan attach/detach semantics updated. Usage records will carry 'band_id' and 'enforcement_reason' tags. Billing pipeline: ingest band_id and adjustments and emit correction transactions as separate invoice line items. Backwards compatibility: clients that ignore band fields will still be billed under fallback semantics.
acceptance_test_steps: 1) Create a test plan with three bands and simulated baseline traffic. Verify band metadata returned by API.
2) Drive traffic to exceed baseline by 4x; validate detector fires within 5 minutes and Console displays transition.
3) Confirm enforcement: subsequent requests are paced and receive expected 429/Retry-After or slowed responses consistent with leaky-bucket behavior.
4) Validate automated crediting: run replayed anomalous spend and confirm credit line-item appears in billing dev ledger and reconciliation job marks it as credited.
5) Test manual override RBAC: operator can lift circuit-breaker for a tenant; action recorded in audit log and owner notified.
6) Run performance regression: verify median token scoring overhead <5ms.
7) End-to-end sanity: generate an invoice for test tenant that includes normal usage, elevated pacing surcharge lines, and corrective credits; verify ledger consistency.
